title: Anomaly Matching and Categorical Classification Frontier

items.title: Exact background-coupled RG comparison
items.design_state: A-page finite-regulator definition of an exact background-coupled Wilsonian comparison with fixed symmetry, background groupoid, field content, measure, and local-counterterm relation; no continuum existence claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$, a compact smooth oriented Euclidean $d$-manifold $M$ with no boundary, its tangential structure (including a spin structure when the fields require one), and the model's boundary conditions. Let $\Gamma=(X,E_\Gamma)$ be the chosen finite regulator graph, with finite vertex set $X$. Fix a compact internal symmetry group $G$ with its actual global form and its action on every retained and integrated field multiplet. The symmetry is global, not a dynamical gauge redundancy. A **background groupoid** $\mathscr B$ is a category in which every arrow is invertible; its objects are the admitted nondynamical $G$-background data and its arrows are exactly the permitted background gauge transformations, including large transformations when the model admits them. The background data, local parameter charts on its object space, groupoid objects and arrows are part of the model input.

At each positive Wilsonian scale $\mu$ in a fixed interval $0<\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}<\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$, specify a finite-dimensional field configuration space $\Phi_\mu$ as a standard Borel space equipped with a model-chosen Polish topology $\tau_\mu$ that generates its standard Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and with a positive normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_\mu$ on $\Phi_\mu$. Its finite retained coordinate set is denoted $L_\mu$; on each sector component the continuous field coordinates are $\mathbb R^{L_\mu}$ with their Euclidean topology, and any topology and measurable structure on admitted sector labels are part of the model data. The chosen topology $\tau_\mu$ is used whenever a low-field open set or continuity in low fields is specified. For every background object $b\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathscr B)$, supply a dimensionless Borel complex weight $w_\mu(-;b)\in L^1(\Phi_\mu,\nu_\mu)$. The weight is primary and may vanish. When a finite Borel action $S_\mu(-;b):\Phi_\mu\to\mathbb C$ is supplied, its weight is $w_\mu=e^{-S_\mu}$; an integrated weight need not admit such an action globally. On each stated smooth local parameter chart of backgrounds, require $b\mapsto Z_\mu[b]$ below to be continuous in the chart topology. Define the finite partition functional by

$$
Z_\mu[b]=\int_{\Phi_\mu}w_\mu(\phi;b)\,d\nu_\mu(\phi)\in\mathbb C.
$$

Require $Z_\mu[b]\ne0$ on every background patch where the effective functional is used. On each such patch choose a continuous branch $\operatorname{Log}_\mu$ and set $W_\mu[b]=-\operatorname{Log}_\mu Z_\mu[b]$; retain the transition phases when branches change on overlaps. If the action is real-valued, the integral is positive and this is the usual real-action case. For complex weights, the integral and background logarithm are the explicitly specified extension of the finite-regulator Wilsonian integral; the supplier definition for real Borel actions alone does not establish integrability or nonvanishing. All field representations, regulator data, measures, normalizations, actions, scale-dependent coordinate splits and background boundary conditions are fixed model inputs.

More precisely, a **finite-regulator Wilsonian high/low integration** is specified at each step of a finite scale chain $\mu_0=\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}>\mu_1>\cdots>\mu_n=\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ (a single step is allowed). At step $j$, the retained coordinate set at scale $\mu_j$ is split as $L_{\mu_j}=L_{\mu_{j+1}}\sqcup H_j$. On each sector component, the associated Borel product identification is $\Phi_{\mu_j}\cong\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}\times\mathbb R^{H_j}$, and the scale measures factor as $\nu_{\mu_j}=\nu_{\mu_{j+1}}\otimes\nu_{H,j}$, where $\nu_{H,j}$ is a normalized Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{H_j}$. Use the Wilsonian matching-scale label $\mu_W=\mu_{j+1}$. The finite-regulator model-data supplier specifies retained and integrated spaces $\mathbb R^X$ and a real Borel ultraviolet action; its Wilsonian-action supplier defines the corresponding high-coordinate integral where it is finite and positive. Arbitrary finite coordinate sets $L_{\mu_{j+1}}$ and $H_j$, admitted sector labels, and complex actions here are additional supplied model data extending that real-action setting. When the optional Gaussian submodel is selected, its $\mathbb R^X$ field spaces and its $M>0$, $E\geq0$, $\Lambda>0$, $A$, and $J$ satisfy the supplier's stated spectral, range, and cutoff conditions. For each fixed background $b$, absolute integrability of $w_{\mu_j}(-;b)$ and the product-measure identification give, by Fubini, a Borel conull subset $F_{j,b}\subseteq\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}$ on which the high-coordinate integral is absolutely convergent. Define the integrated weight by

$$
q_{j,b}(\ell)=\int_{\mathbb R^{H_j}}w_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)\,d\nu_{H,j}(h)\quad(\ell\in F_{j,b}),\qquad w_{\mu_{j+1}}(\ell;b)=e^{c_j[b]}q_{j,b}(\ell),
$$

where $c_j[b]$ is the declared dimensionless local background counterterm assigned to that step (zero is allowed). On the exceptional Borel null set choose a finite Borel extension of $q_{j,b}$, for example zero; its value does not affect any partition functional. These assertions are for each fixed $b$; any additional regularity jointly in backgrounds is supplied model data. The resulting low weight is integrable because $|q_{j,b}(\ell)|\le\int|w_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)|\,d\nu_{H,j}(h)$ almost everywhere. Its zero locus is allowed, including a set of positive low-field measure.

A field-action description is additional local data. On an open patch in the product of the declared low-field topology and a background-chart topology where a chosen representative of $q_{j,b}(\ell)$ is continuous and nonzero and admits a continuous logarithm, choose such a branch and define only on that patch

$$
S_{\mu_{j+1}}(\ell;b)=-\operatorname{Log}q_{j,b}(\ell)-c_j[b].
$$

Where an ultraviolet action is supplied, $q_{j,b}(\ell)=\int e^{-S_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)}\,d\nu_{H,j}(h)$, so this is the original local Wilsonian logarithm formula. For real actions and $c_j=0$, with the real logarithm and field data in the suppliers' domain, it agrees with the supplied Wilsonian-action definition. No local-action patches are required to cover a zero locus. For fixed $b$, a global finite Borel action representing a chosen Borel low weight exists exactly when that representative is nowhere zero: necessity follows from $e^{-S}\ne0$, and sufficiency from the Borel logarithm $\log|w|+i\operatorname{Arg}(w)$ with $\operatorname{Arg}\in(-\pi,\pi]$. A finite Borel action representing the weight almost everywhere exists exactly when it is nonzero almost everywhere, with arbitrary finite action on the exceptional null set. A continuous global action requires, in addition, a continuous logarithm of the nonvanishing weight; nonvanishing alone does not guarantee this. Scale measures are compatible products, so every partition functional is the corresponding iterated finite integral, whether or not a global action exists. Every retained field and every retained topological sector is included at $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$.

With these product measures, Fubini and the integrated-weight definition give the global identity $Z_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=e^{c_j[b]}Z_{\mu_j}[b]$, including all low-field zero loci. On nonvanishing background patches, compatible logarithm branches then give $W_{\mu_j}[b]-W_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=c_j[b]$. Choose the logarithm branches compatibly along the chain; any transitions between local background patches retain their transition phases.

For each background-groupoid arrow, the model supplies the Borel identifications of the field spaces and the induced pullbacks on local partition branches. Each high-coordinate weight-integration map must intertwine those pullbacks (as equalities of integrable weights modulo null sets), including the induced branch-transition phases wherever logarithmic descriptions exist; this is equivariance of the integration map and does not assert that each local scalar partition branch is gauge invariant. An **exact background-coupled RG comparison** is such a finite sequence of integrations for which the sum $C[b]=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j[b]$ is a single-valued admissible dimensionless local background functional and

$$
W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[b]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[b]=C[b]
$$

on each common local branch and compatibly on overlaps. Here local means an integral or finite-regulator sum of densities depending on background data and finitely many derivatives or neighboring cochains; the allowed counterterm space is fixed as part of the model. This definition records a finite-regulator flow interface and its locality hypothesis. It does not assert that such a flow exists for an arbitrary continuum QFT or that any continuum limit exists.

items.title: Symmetry-preserving RG anomaly matching
items.design_state: A-page conditional equality of the selected anomaly class along the declared exact symmetry-preserving background flow, modulo the stated local counterterms and global holonomies; no phase exclusion or continuum claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Assume Countable Choice: every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Fix a finite-regulator model on a compact, closed, oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold $M$, with its actual boundary-condition data, fields and jets, regulator, measure, and admissible local counterterms at every scale. Let $G$ be a compact finite-dimensional real Lie group serving as the internal global symmetry with fixed global form, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $G$-bundle with supplied smooth connection $A$, let $V_R$ be a finite-dimensional Hermitian complex vector space, and let $R:G\to U(V_R)$ be a smooth group homomorphism. The admitted background groupoid has these nondynamical connections as objects and the selected background gauge transformations as arrows; the symmetry is exact and unbroken along the flow and is not a dynamical gauge redundancy. Fix a smooth family of Fredholm chiral Dirac operators $D^+_{A,R}$ and its inverse determinant line with the Quillen metric and Bismut–Freed unitary connection, with precisely the spin/Clifford, associated-bundle, induced-connection, Sobolev-domain, and admissible spectral-cut/regularization conventions of the determinant-line definition. On each background patch, the finite-regulator partition functional at scale $\mu$ is the local scalar representative of a section of that line, and its transition functions and endpoint gauge actions are retained.

Also fix a Minkowski coordinate region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with its orientation, spin structure, boundary-term convention, fields and jet domains, and identify it with the Euclidean local-variation problem by a specified Wick-rotation map. Here that map means an isomorphism between the complexified local background finite-jet algebras on the two patches, mapping the admitted background fields and horizontal forms and intertwining the horizontal derivatives and BRST differentials while preserving the declared boundary-term convention. Use the Minkowski patch's background-only finite-jet BRST complex, with nilpotent differential $s$ and horizontal derivative $d_H$; its local anomaly class is the relative cohomology class of ghost-number-one horizontal four-form cocycles modulo $d_H$ and the declared four-dimensional background counterterms. Write $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for the background-only finite-jet local density whose integral on this patch is the counterterm $C$. Assume an exact symmetry-preserving Wilsonian comparison from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ retains all remaining low-energy and topological sectors and satisfies $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[A]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[A]=C[A]$ on each common local branch, for one admissible, single-valued, dimensionless local counterterm.

For the local anomaly conclusion, impose the following additional compatibility hypothesis. In the same regularization and boundary-term convention at both endpoints, the infinitesimal BRST variation of each branch $W_\mu$ is local in finite jets and is represented by the corresponding $a_{\mu,4}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ used in the local-anomaly definition: $\delta_s W_\mu[A]=\int_U a_{\mu,4}$ modulo the fixed boundary term. The specified Wick-rotation map carries these Euclidean variations to that BRST complex and commutes with its differential. The representative assignment is linear on the common branches, and the local counterterm assignment is compatible with it, so replacing a branch by that branch plus $C[A]=\int_U\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ changes its representative by $s\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}+d_Hq_3$ with $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathcal C$ and $q_3\in\mathcal N$, where the same declared counterterm and boundary spaces $\mathcal C,\mathcal N$ are used at both endpoints. This is model and regularization data; it is not inferred from the scalar partition equality alone.

For the determinant-line comparison, take $C$ in the unitary phase convention so $e^{-C[A]}\in U(1)$. Assume the line-valued comparison induces a unitary isomorphism of the endpoint determinant-line families which, in local frames, is multiplication by the phase $e^{-C[A]}$ and which preserves the specified unitary connections and endpoint gauge identifications. Then the ultraviolet and complete infrared four-dimensional local BRST anomaly classes agree modulo the declared local counterterms, and the determinant-line holonomies agree on every admitted loop of background connections modulo gauge transformations. This is a conditional matching constraint only; it determines no infrared spectrum or gap and asserts no continuum limit or empirical result.

No continuum limit, phase exclusion, spectrum claim, or empirical result is asserted.

items.title: Anomaly matching structures for fusion 2-categories
items.design_state: Status-reviewed bounded 2+1d bosonic fusion-2-category anomaly-matching classification question; the earlier 3+1d/fusion-2-category lead is corrected to the dimension supported by the current sources.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an oriented bosonic $2+1$-dimensional theory. Throughout this problem use **weak monoidal 2-categories**, with the following explicit convention. The underlying $\mathbb C$-linear 2-category is strict as in the earlier defect-fusion definition: composition of 1-morphisms is strictly associative and unital and horizontal and vertical composition of 2-morphisms satisfy interchange. Weakness here concerns the tensor structure; it does not mean discarding any coherence maps.

The tensor is a $\mathbb C$-bilinear pseudofunctor $\otimes:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, with a unit object $I_{\mathcal A}$. A linear pseudofunctor assigns objects and linear functors on Hom categories, with invertible comparison 2-morphisms $F(g)\circ F(f)\Rightarrow F(g\circ f)$ and $1_{F(X)}\Rightarrow F(1_X)$. The two composites of comparison maps on a triple of composable 1-morphisms agree, the identity comparisons satisfy the two unit equations, and all comparisons are natural in 2-morphisms. These requirements apply to the tensor pseudofunctor too, so tensor interchange is retained.

The monoidal structure includes pseudonatural adjoint equivalences $a_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$, $l_X:I_{\mathcal A}\otimes X\to X$, and $r_X:X\otimes I_{\mathcal A}\to X$. A pseudonatural transformation has a 1-morphism component at each object and an invertible naturality 2-morphism at each 1-morphism, natural in 2-morphisms and compatible with composition and identities. An adjoint equivalence includes a chosen inverse and invertible unit and counit modifications satisfying the triangle identities. A modification has 2-morphism components whose naturality squares commute. There is an invertible pentagonator modification
$$
\pi_{W,X,Y,Z}:(1_W\otimes a_{X,Y,Z})\circ a_{W,X\otimes Y,Z}\circ(a_{W,X,Y}\otimes1_Z)\Longrightarrow a_{W,X,Y\otimes Z}\circ a_{W\otimes X,Y,Z},
$$
and invertible unit modifications, here written in the equivalent orientations
$$
\lambda_{X,Y}:l_{X\otimes Y}\circ a_{I_{\mathcal A},X,Y}\Longrightarrow l_X\otimes1_Y,\qquad \rho_{X,Y}:r_{X\otimes Y}\Longrightarrow(1_X\otimes r_Y)\circ a_{X,Y,I_{\mathcal A}},
$$
$$
\mu_{X,Y}:(1_X\otimes l_Y)\circ a_{X,I_{\mathcal A},Y}\Longrightarrow r_X\otimes1_Y.
$$
Require the monoidal-bicategory coherence axioms: the two pastings of pentagonators around the five-object associahedron agree; the unit modifications satisfy the triangle and double-unit pasting equations and their compatibility with the pentagonator, with the tensor pseudofunctor comparisons and naturality cells inserted. Equivalently these data, with the underlying 2-category as the single Hom bicategory, form a one-object tricategory. This is the weak monoidal-bicategory convention used by Kong–Tian–Zhou in §2; no associator, unitor, tensor comparison or pentagonator is required to be an identity. In particular the pentagonator is a specified 2-isomorphism between the displayed parallel 1-morphisms, and neither equality of those composites nor an identity 2-morphism is required.

Each of $\mathcal N$, the fixed marked $\mathcal C$, and $\mathcal S$ has this weak tensor structure. Finite semisimplicity, adjoints and separable splittings have exactly the underlying-2-category meanings in the earlier defect-fusion definition: Hom categories are finite semisimple $\mathbb C$-linear categories, all 1-morphisms have both adjoints, finite object direct sums exist, separable monads split, and there are finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects. Each object also has left and right tensor duals, with evaluation, coevaluation and invertible cusp 2-morphisms comparing the two triangle composites to identities; the chosen $a,l,r$ are inserted in those composites. The tensor unit is simple. Thus only the earlier definition's Gray-monoid tensor convention is replaced here. No dagger, positivity, unitarity, or physical realization is implied. A supplied physical realization interprets objects, 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms as surface defects, line junctions and point junctions respectively.

A **linear monoidal 2-functor** in this problem is a linear pseudofunctor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of the underlying 2-categories, with a pseudonatural adjoint equivalence $\chi_{X,Y}:F(X)\otimes F(Y)\to F(X\otimes Y)$ and a unit adjoint equivalence $\iota:I_{\mathcal B}\to F(I_{\mathcal A})$. It includes invertible associativity and left- and right-unit modifications: the associativity modification compares the two composites from $(F(X)\otimes F(Y))\otimes F(Z)$ to $F(X\otimes(Y\otimes Z))$ using $a_{\mathcal B},\chi$ on one route and $\chi,F(a_{\mathcal A})$ on the other. The unit modifications compare $l_{F(X)}$ and $r_{F(X)}$ to the routes using $\iota,\chi,F(l_X),F(r_X)$. Require their four-object pentagonator-compatibility equation and unit-compatibility equations with $\lambda,\rho,\mu$, including every pseudofunctor comparison. These are equalities of 2-morphism pastings; in particular they preserve the possibly nonidentity $\pi$.

A monoidal pseudonatural transformation between these functors has pseudonatural 1-morphism components and invertible modifications comparing $\chi$ and $\iota$ on the two sides, satisfying the associativity and unit compatibility equations. It is an equivalence when its components are equivalence 1-morphisms, with inverse and unit/counit monoidal modifications supplied. Monoidal modifications preserve those tensor and unit comparisons. A monoidal 2-equivalence has an inverse up to these monoidal pseudonatural equivalences and modifications. Use this same weak convention for all center, boundary, interface, transport and endpoint data below; none are replaced by strict models.

Here **all-boson type** means obtainable by the following generalized-gauging construction from finite ordinary group data: choose a finite group $G$, a normalized group 4-cocycle $\omega:G^4\to U(1)$ representing $[\omega]\in H^4(BG;U(1))$, a finite subgroup $H\leq G$, and an oriented bosonic three-dimensional topological theory with specified $H$-symmetry data. The $H$-symmetry data are a homotopy-coherent action of $H$ on its topological defect data by invertible defect functors, including the associated degree-four $U(1)$ anomaly class. Stack the theories and gauge the diagonal $H$ only when the total $H$ anomaly cancels, so summing over diagonal $H$ backgrounds is defined. The complete stacked theory, the cancellation data, and the resulting boundary data are retained, including nonminimal choices and noninvertible phases. A finite group is viewed through its classifying space $BG$, so the stated cohomology is ordinary group cohomology with trivial $U(1)$ coefficients. Each of $\mathcal N,\mathcal C,\mathcal S$ is supplied with a chosen such finite-group presentation, denoted $(G_{\mathcal A},\omega_{\mathcal A})$ together with its full gauging and boundary data; this choice is part of the marking.

For this input, $2\mathrm{Vec}^{\omega}_G$ denotes the $\mathbb C$-linear monoidal 2-category of finite semisimple $G$-graded $\mathbb C$-linear categories, grade-preserving linear functors, and natural transformations. Its tensor product is the graded tensor product: the degree-$g$ summand of $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B$ is $\bigoplus_{xy=g}\mathcal A_x\boxtimes\mathcal B_y$, where $\boxtimes$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear Deligne product of finite semisimple categories; its tensor unit is finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector spaces concentrated in the identity grade. Use the canonical tensor comparisons, rebracketing associator and unitors, with their normalized unit modifications. The monoidal pentagonator $\pi$ on four homogeneous grades $g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4$ is multiplied by $\omega(g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4)$; the five-object coherence is exactly
$$
\omega(h,k,l,m)\omega(g,hk,l,m)\omega(g,h,k,lm)=\omega(gh,k,l,m)\omega(g,h,kl,m)\omega(g,h,k,l).
$$
Normalization means $\omega(g,h,k,l)=1$ whenever one argument is the identity, and supplies the unit compatibilities. These are the nonsemistrict models themselves; a nonidentity scalar pentagonator is not removed. A normalized cocycle representative is part of the presentation, while cohomologous representatives are compared only through a specified monoidal 2-equivalence.

Write $Z_2(\mathcal A)$ for the Drinfeld center of a monoidal 2-category $\mathcal A$: an object is an object $X\in\mathcal A$ equipped with a pseudonatural equivalence $X\otimes(-)\simeq(-)\otimes X$ and invertible unit and tensor-compatibility modifications satisfying the weak center pasting axiom (2.1) of Kong–Tian–Zhou, with the associators, tensor comparisons and pentagonators retained, and its unit specialization; 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms preserve that structure by the modification and 2-morphism equations (2.2) and (2.3) of that source. In particular this is its nonsemistrict center, whose coherence depends on $\pi$; it is not the center computed after suppressing $\pi$. It is a braided monoidal 2-category. Distinguish this defect category from the selected oriented $3+1$-dimensional SymTFT, denoted $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal A}$. The latter is a fully extended oriented 4-dimensional topological field theory; here fully extended means a symmetric monoidal assignment to oriented bordisms with defect strata down to points, with a fixed target higher category and gluing equivalences. Its bulk surface, line, and point defects form the specified braided 2-category $Z_2(\mathcal A)$. For the chosen all-boson presentation, take $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal A}$ to be the finite-group Dijkgraaf-Witten theory $\mathrm{DW}_4(G_{\mathcal A},\omega_{\mathcal A})$: its fields on a manifold are flat principal finite-$G_{\mathcal A}$ bundles, and a closed oriented 4-manifold with bundle classified by $f:Y\to BG_{\mathcal A}$ has cocycle weight $\langle f^*\omega_{\mathcal A},[Y]\rangle\in U(1)$, with the theory summing over bundles with its fixed gauge-volume normalization. The chosen identification between $Z_2(\mathcal A)$ and these bulk-defect data is part of the marking; no such identification is inferred from an abstract category alone.

A symmetry boundary $B_{\mathcal A}$ is a selected topological boundary condition of $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal A}$ with its full finite semisimple 2-category of boundary surface, line, and point defects, the action of bulk defects on that 2-category, and all tensor, composition, and junction maps with their weak associativity, unit and pentagonator compatibilities. A topological interface $\mathcal I_{\mathcal A\to\mathcal B}$ is a selected codimension-one wall between $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal A}$ and $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal B}$, equivalently a boundary condition for the folded theory $\overline{\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal A}}\otimes\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal B}$, together with its complete finite semisimple defect 2-category, bulk-defect actions, and endpoint data. Here "gapped" means precisely that the selected boundary or wall is topological and has the stated finite semisimple defect data; it asserts no property of a microscopic theory.

Make the boundary and wall actions and their vacua explicit as follows. For each selected boundary $D$, let $\mathcal M_D$ be its marked finite semisimple $\mathbb C$-linear defect 2-category, with boundary surfaces as objects, line junctions as 1-morphisms, and point junctions as 2-morphisms. Mark a nonzero vacuum surface object $b_D\in\mathcal M_D$; it need not be simple, so nonminimal boundary data are retained. Supply a weak bulk action $\triangleright:\mathcal B_D\times\mathcal M_D\to\mathcal M_D$, where $\mathcal B_D$ is the relevant bulk defect 2-category. This is a $\mathbb C$-bilinear pseudofunctor, linear in each variable, with pseudonatural adjoint equivalences $(x\otimes y)\triangleright m\simeq x\triangleright(y\triangleright m)$ and $\mathbf1\triangleright m\simeq m$, and invertible associativity and unit modifications. Require the module pentagon and unit pasting equations, including the actual bulk associator, unitors, pentagonator, tensor comparisons and action comparisons. These action and coherence data are supplied, not inferred from defect labels. For an interface use its folded wall-defect 2-category $\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}$ and a marked nonzero vacuum surface $b_{\mathcal I}$, with the selected side's action obtained from its supplied full folded bulk action, retaining its orientation conventions.

For a bulk surface sector $x$, the acted-on object $x\triangleright b_D$ is a boundary surface object. Define the **endpoint category**
$$
E_D(x):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M_D}(x\triangleright b_D,b_D).
$$
Its objects are endpoint line junctions $e:x\triangleright b_D\to b_D$, and its morphisms are actual point junctions $\alpha:e\Rightarrow e'$. These morphism spaces are the original complex vector spaces of 2-morphisms, with their bilinear vertical composition. Thus $E_D(x)$ is finite semisimple and linear by the stipulated Hom-category property of $\mathcal M_D$. Say that $x$ is **endable** at $D$ exactly when this category has a nonzero object, equivalently a nonzero simple object. A zero 1-morphism is always present but is not an endability witness; the category is zero when all its objects are isomorphic to that zero 1-morphism. The vacuum sector is endable: the supplied unit equivalence $\mathbf1\triangleright b_D\simeq b_D$ is a nonzero endpoint line, since $b_D$ is nonzero. There is no identity-line witness for an arbitrary $x$, because its endpoint lines have the specified source $x\triangleright b_D$ and target $b_D$.

The bulk action gives a linear pseudofunctor $E_D:\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{op}}\to2\mathrm{Vect}$, where $\mathrm{op}$ reverses 1-morphisms but keeps the direction of 2-morphisms, and $2\mathrm{Vect}$ has finite semisimple linear categories, linear functors and natural transformations. Explicitly, $f:x\to y$ acts by the linear functor $E_D(y)\to E_D(x)$ sending $e$ to $e\circ(f\triangleright1_{b_D})$, and $\alpha:f\Rightarrow g$ acts by the natural transformation with component $e\star(\alpha\triangleright1_{b_D})$, where $\star$ denotes whiskering. The action pseudofunctor comparisons give the endpoint identity and composition comparisons; their equations follow the supplied action equations, with no strict replacement. Endpoint fusion sends $(e,e')\in E_D(x)\times E_D(y)$ to the composite
$$
(x\otimes y)\triangleright b_D\longrightarrow x\triangleright(y\triangleright b_D)\xrightarrow{x\triangleright e'}x\triangleright b_D\xrightarrow{e}b_D.
$$
It acts on point junctions by whiskering and composition and is bilinear; its unit is the displayed vacuum endpoint. Its associativity, unit and bulk-junction comparisons retain the supplied weak action coherence, including the pentagonator. No claim that fusion of two nonzero endpoint lines is always nonzero is made.

A marked interface includes its defect-transport linear monoidal 2-functor $T:\mathcal B_D\to\mathcal B_{D'}$, a linear module pseudofunctor $U:\mathcal M_D\to\mathcal M_{D'}$, and a specified adjoint equivalence $u:U(b_D)\simeq b_{D'}$. Here module structure means pseudonatural adjoint equivalences $\beta_{x,m}:U(x\triangleright m)\to T(x)\triangleright U(m)$ with invertible composition, tensor and unit modifications satisfying the action-compatibility pasting equations; retain all comparisons of $T,U$ and the two actions. Its endpoint transport sends $e\in E_D(x)$ to
$$
u\circ U(e)\circ\beta_{x,b_D}^{-1}\circ(T(x)\triangleright u^{-1})\in E_{D'}(Tx),
$$
with the specified adjoint inverses and pseudofunctor comparisons inserted. On point junctions it applies $U$ and the same whiskerings, so it preserves their actual linear combinations and amplitudes. Module coherence supplies its comparisons with bulk 1- and 2-morphisms and endpoint fusion; require every resulting composition, tensor and vacuum pasting to commute. The marking also includes the specified equivalence of transported source boundary defect data with target boundary defect data, preserving these module actions and vacuum markings. These structures are required data of an admissible marked diagram, not a universal construction of transport or a physical realization theorem. This Hom-category endpoint formulation is an owner-selected precise encoding of the source's endability proposal; it is not asserted equivalent to a category of chosen point-junction pairs with affine intertwining arrows.

Fix $\mathcal C$ and its particular boundary realization $B_{\mathcal C}$. Consider marked diagrams $\mathcal N\xrightarrow{I}\mathcal C\xrightarrow{P}\mathcal S$ of the above categories and linear monoidal 2-functors, with chosen boundaries $B_{\mathcal N},B_{\mathcal S}$ and chosen interfaces $\mathcal I_I,\mathcal I_P$ realizing $I,P$. The marking includes the wall-induced transport functors and boundary identifications just defined. Classify the equivalence classes of these diagrams satisfying all three conditions below.

1. For every simple surface sector $x\in Z_2(\mathcal C)$, if $E_{B_{\mathcal C}}(x)$ is nonzero then $E_{\mathcal I_I}(x)$ on the $\mathcal C$ side is nonzero.

2. If a simple sector $x\in Z_2(\mathcal C)$ is endable both on $B_{\mathcal C}$ and on the $\mathcal C$ side of $\mathcal I_P$, then $x$ is equivalent to the tensor unit. Thus the intersection of the two sets of jointly endable simple sectors contains only the tensor unit. This condition says nothing about a non-simple direct sum containing one summand endable on $B_{\mathcal C}$ and a different summand endable on the $\mathcal C$ side of $\mathcal I_P$, with no jointly endable summand.

3. The composite $T_{\mathcal I_P}T_{\mathcal I_I}$ identifies $Z_2(\mathcal N)$ with the full replete additive sub-2-category of $Z_2(\mathcal S)$ generated by the simple surface sectors endable on $B_{\mathcal S}$. Require that subcategory to contain the tensor unit and be closed under the tensor product; this is not inferred from the endability predicate alone. This identification is a monoidal 2-equivalence on that subcategory and induces linear equivalences of the corresponding Hom-category endpoint data, preserving their actual line objects, point-junction vector spaces, bulk-junction action, endpoint fusion and vacuum comparisons.

The research problem is to prove the coherent categorical form of these conditions, show that it is invariant under the marked equivalence, and determine the intrinsic formulation in monoidal 2-functor language, including which notions of kernel, normality, embedding, dominance, and exactness it actually induces. Do not assume ordinary fusion-category definitions extend unchanged, or that a unique maximal anomaly-free full sub-2-category exists.

An equivalence between two marked diagrams consists of monoidal 2-equivalences of their $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal S$ entries, the identity on the fixed marked $\mathcal C$ and $B_{\mathcal C}$ including its module action and vacuum surface, monoidal pseudonatural equivalences identifying the two copies of $I$ and $P$, and equivalences of the remaining selected SymTFTs, boundaries, interfaces, and endpoint data. On boundary and wall defect data require module 2-equivalences with specified adjoint equivalences of the vacuum surfaces, compatible with the chosen $U,\beta,u$ and their comparisons. Their induced Hom-category equivalences must preserve the actual linear point-junction maps and endpoint fusion, not just nonzero support. These equivalences must intertwine every bulk-defect action and boundary identification; modifications must preserve all composition, tensor and vacuum coherences. The classification is not equality merely of fusion rules, abstract defect labels, or endpoint existence predicates.

The source-backed finite-group benchmark, in this same weak convention, is a short exact sequence of finite groups $1\to N\to G\xrightarrow{p}Q=G/N\to1$, with $N$ normal, and a normalized cocycle $\omega:Q^4\to U(1)$. Pullback gives $p^*\omega\in Z^4(G;U(1))$ and the sequence is $2\mathrm{Vec}_N\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{p^*\omega}_G\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{\omega}_Q$ with its associated condensation interface; identify it in the marked-interface formulation above. Explicitly the inclusion extends an $N$-graded category by zero to $G$, while the quotient sends a $G$-graded category $\mathcal A$ to the $Q$-graded category with component $\bigoplus_{p(g)=q}\mathcal A_g$ at $q$. Both act componentwise on functors and natural transformations; their tensor equivalences are the canonical reindexing and distributivity equivalences of finite sums and Deligne products. For the inclusion, $(p^*\omega)(n_1,n_2,n_3,n_4)=\omega(e,e,e,e)=1$; for the quotient, $(p^*\omega)(g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4)=\omega(p(g_1),p(g_2),p(g_3),p(g_4))$. Hence the scalar pentagonators on each homogeneous summand agree under these functors. The remaining comparison pastings are the same canonical reindexings of elementary tensors, so agree on every summand, and normalization gives the unit compatibilities. This specifies their weak monoidal functor data without a strictification step and retains arbitrary normalized $\omega$, including nontrivial cohomology classes. A **finite 2-group** here is a monoidal groupoid with finitely many isomorphism classes of objects and finite automorphism groups, all objects tensor-invertible; equivalently its classifying space is a connected 2-type with finite $\pi_1$, finite abelian $\pi_2$, the $\pi_1$-action on $\pi_2$, and a Postnikov class in $H^3(\pi_1;\pi_2)$. A short exact sequence $1\to\mathbf H\to\mathbf G\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf K\to1$ means a homotopy-fiber sequence $B\mathbf H\to B\mathbf G\to B\mathbf K$, retaining these action and Postnikov data even when nonsplit. For $[\omega]\in H^4(B\mathbf K;U(1))$, determine whether and under what hypotheses the proposed analogue $2\mathrm{Vec}_{\mathbf H}\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{p^*\omega}_{\mathbf G}\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{\omega}_{\mathbf K}$ exists and is exact. The notation $2\mathrm{Vec}^{\omega}_{\mathbf G}$ for a finite 2-group denotes the candidate to be constructed: its objects should be finite semisimple categories graded by the 2-type $B\mathbf G$ with coherent 4-cocycle-twisted monoidal structure. Its precise construction and exactness are open, not prerequisites or assumed results.

Is the complete marked endability and transport invariant above sufficient to classify the interface equivalence classes? If not, exhibit inequivalent finite semisimple marked interfaces with identical proposed invariant and identify the additional junction or coherence datum required. This is not a classification of gapped phases or abstract fusion 2-categories alone, and no finite enumeration of boundary choices is assumed.

As a further compatibility problem, define a categorical background on an oriented 3-manifold by a stratified surface/line/point defect network whose strata are labelled by objects, 1-morphisms, and 2-morphisms of $\mathcal C$ and whose junctions obey the stated composition and tensor coherences. Construct its relative bulk response as the functorial state and junction data of $\mathfrak Z_{\mathcal C}$, including gluing maps, and identify the full sub-2-category generated by tensor-invertible bulk sectors and invertible junctions; call this the invertible subsector. General SymTFTs can be noninvertible and require categorical state and junction spaces, so scalar local variations, line holonomies, and invertible inflow are not asserted to classify the full response. On ordinary backgrounds where the earlier suppliers' hypotheses apply, the invertible restriction should reproduce the background-only finite-jet $H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H)$ class modulo counterterms, the holonomy of the inverse determinant line of a smooth Fredholm chiral Dirac family with its unitary connection around a background loop including its endpoint gauge arrow, and the cancellation of boundary-line holonomy against the dual spin-bulk line respectively. Those earlier interfaces neither construct these oriented $2+1$-dimensional categorical backgrounds nor prove this extension. No classification, physical realization of an arbitrary abstract diagram, or anomaly-matching theorem is asserted here.

items.title: A mixed-background counterterm shift along RG
items.design_state: B-page worked small-gauge U(1)^3 background counterterm variation on a closed four-torus; verifies equality of the four-dimensional local anomaly classes.
items.statement:
Let $M=T^4$ be a closed flat Euclidean four-torus. Fix three nondynamical $U(1)$ background connections $A_1,A_2,A_3$, each a globally defined real 1-form on the trivial bundle, and allow only gauge transformations $A_i\mapsto A_i+d\lambda_i$ with smooth single-valued periodic dimensionless real functions $\lambda_i$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, so $[A_i]=$ mass, $[F_i]=$ mass squared, and the functional below is dimensionless. For interpreting endpoint anomaly representatives, assume the model specifies the same Wick-rotation isomorphism between complexified Minkowski and Euclidean local background finite-jet algebras as in the symmetry-preserving RG matching theorem; it maps these fields and horizontal forms and intertwines the BRST differentials and the fixed boundary-term convention. Assume also that the same regularized local BRST-variation assignment at both endpoints identifies each endpoint anomaly representative with the variation of its own $W_\mu$ branch in that finite-jet complex, is linear on common branches, and sends a local counterterm density to its BRST variation modulo a $d_H$-exact form. This is additional model data; the scalar RG identity and the calculation below do not supply that identification or compatibility. In a declared counterterm scheme, take the allowed local background counterterm, with $F_i:=dA_i$ and $d$ the exterior derivative on $T^4$.

$$
C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4} A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3,
$$

where $k\in\mathbb R$ is a fixed dimensionless coefficient. In the common local scheme require $\mathcal C_k=\frac{ik}{2\pi}A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3\in\mathcal C$ and require the boundary primitive $q_3$ supplied by the endpoint BRST-variation identification to belong to the same space $\mathcal N$ at both endpoints; the closed-torus convention discards its total derivative. Suppose an exact background-coupled RG comparison has $W_{\mathrm{UV}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]=W_{\mathrm{IR}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]+C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]$ on this background domain. Then the gauge variation of the counterterm is

$$
\delta C_k=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4}\bigl(-\lambda_1 F_2\wedge F_3+\lambda_2 F_1\wedge F_3\bigr),\qquad F_i=dA_i,
$$

Here $s$ and $d_H$ are the nilpotent differential and horizontal derivative of the background-only finite-jet BRST complex in the local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly definition; $H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H)$ is its ghost-number-one four-form cocycle quotient by total derivatives and the declared counterterms. The integrand in the displayed gauge variation is the gauge-parameter evaluation of the local counterterm variation. The common regularized BRST assignment in the preceding hypothesis lifts this variation to the ghost-number-one local representative modulo $d_H$, so the endpoint representatives define the same local anomaly class; the gauge-variation formula alone does not make that identification.

items.title: A fixed source breaks the matching symmetry
items.design_state: B-page finite four-dimensional scalar-lattice endpoint with a fixed source; checks explicit breaking and the failure of the theorem hypothesis.
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda_a=(a\mathbb Z/Na\mathbb Z)^4$ be the periodic four-dimensional lattice with $N\geq2$ sites in each direction and spacing $a>0$; each coordinate is taken modulo $Na$. At each site $x$ take a complex scalar $\phi_x$ of mass dimension one. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, choose a mass $m_0>0$ and a dimensionless coupling $\lambda>0$, and define the finite Euclidean action

$$
S_j[\phi]=a^4\sum_{x\in\Lambda_a}\left(\sum_{\nu=1}^{4}\left|\frac{\phi_{x+a\hat\nu}-\phi_x}{a}\right|^2+m_0^2|\phi_x|^2+\lambda|\phi_x|^4+j(\phi_x+\overline{\phi_x})\right),
$$

where the fixed real source $j\neq0$ has mass dimension three. The finite-dimensional Lebesgue integral converges because the positive quartic term dominates the linear source. The source-free action has a global $U(1)$ transformation $\phi_x\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\phi_x$, but the fixed-source theory does not. Consequently this endpoint fails the exact-symmetry hypothesis of the anomaly-matching theorem; the example asserts no change, absence, or value of an anomaly.
